title: X-ray diffraction of semiconductor crystals
summary: Cubic semiconductors' cells from the Crystallography Open Database, their Bragg reflections, the selection rule of the diamond and zincblende structures, and the peak splitting that measures epitaxial films.

concepts.label: Crystal structure
concepts.description: A periodic arrangement of atoms; here fcc lattices with a two-atom basis.

children.label: Lattice constant
children.description: Edge a of the cubic cell, in Å, from COD entries.

children.label: Diamond structure
children.description: Two identical atoms per lattice point (Si, Ge, C), space group Fd-3m.

children.label: Zincblende structure
children.description: Two different atoms (GaAs, InP), space group F-43m.

children.label: Crystal defect
children.description: Dislocations and point defects; they broaden peaks and relax strained films.

concepts.label: Bragg reflection
concepts.description: Constructive interference from lattice planes (hkl) at nλ = 2d sin θ.

children.label: Structure factor
children.description: Sum of the atoms' scattered waves in a cell; its square sets the intensity and its zeros the selection rules.

children.label: Atomic scattering factor
children.description: An atom's scattering power, Z at θ = 0 and falling with sin θ / λ; here approximated by Z.

facts.text: Tabulated in the International Tables for Crystallography, Vol. C, Table 6.1.1.4.

children.label: Multiplicity
children.description: Number of equivalent planes in a family {hkl}.

concepts.label: Epitaxial film
concepts.description: A crystalline layer grown on a substrate with the same orientation.

children.label: Lattice mismatch
children.description: (a_film − a_substrate) / a_substrate; below about 0.1–1% a film grows strained without dislocations up to a critical thickness.

children.label: Peak splitting
children.description: Δ2θ between film and substrate peaks, −2 tan θ Δa/a.
